examples.ko: 동생은 눈썰미가 좋아서 한 번만 봐도 따라 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has a quick eye and copies things after seeing them just once.

examples.ko: 눈썰미 있는 직원이 새 일을 금방 배웠어요.
examples.en: The observant employee learned the new job quickly.

examples.ko: 저는 눈썰미가 없어서 길을 자주 잃어버려요.
examples.en: I'm not good at noticing things, so I often get lost.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 원래 눈썰미도 좋고 손끝도 야무져서 소문이 났어요.
examples.en: That friend has always been quick to learn and skilled with their hands, so word got around.

examples.ko: 할머니는 눈썰미가 대단해서 옷을 한 번 보면 똑같이 만드세요.
examples.en: My grandmother has a remarkable eye and can make a garment just like one she has seen once.
I relied only on watching and copying, and I made a mistake.

explain: '눈치'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 눈치는 분위기를 읽는 힘이고 눈썰미는 보고 따라 하는 솜씨예요. '눈썰미가 있다/좋다/없다'로 말하고, '손끝이 야무지다'와 함께 칭찬할 때도 나와요.
explain_en: It is easy to mix up with '눈치' (reading the mood): 눈치 is about sensing the atmosphere, while 눈썰미 is the knack of picking things up by watching. You say '눈썰미가 있다/좋다/없다', and it sometimes appears together with '손끝이 야무지다' when praising someone.

en: thorn in the side; pain in the neck

examples.ko: 그 사람은 팀장님에게 눈엣가시 같은 존재예요.
examples.en: That person is a thorn in the team leader's side.
After I got promoted, I became a thorn in my colleagues' side.

examples.ko: 제가 왜 그 사람한테 눈엣가시인지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I don't know why I'm such an eyesore to that person.
They say the daughter-in-law looked like a thorn in her mother-in-law's side.

examples.ko: 우리 가게 옆에 새로 생긴 가게가 눈엣가시예요.
examples.en: The new shop that opened next to ours is a real thorn in our side.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 반에서 눈엣가시 취급을 받아요.
examples.en: That child is treated like a nuisance in the class.

explain: 보기만 해도 거슬리고 미운 사람이나 일에 써요. '눈엣가시 같다/이다/되다'처럼 말하고, 그냥 귀찮은 일보다 마음에 안 들어서 계속 신경 쓰이는 대상에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used for a person or thing that bothers you just by being seen. You say '눈엣가시 같다/이다/되다', and it fits something you dislike and keep noticing rather than a simple chore.

en: treat to the eye; feast for the eye

examples.en: I just looked around the market without buying anything.
Shall we at least look around the department store before we go?
For expensive bags, just looking is enough for me.
I got a real feast for the eyes from the fireworks at the festival.
There was so much to look at that I never got bored.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 눈요기는 되는데 이야기가 약해요.
examples.en: This movie is a treat for the eyes, but the story is weak.

explain: 사지는 않고 보기만 할 때, 또는 화려한 볼거리를 즐길 때 써요. '눈요기하다'나 '눈요기를 하다'로 말하고, 영화처럼 볼거리만 좋을 때는 살짝 아쉬운 뉘앙스로도 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when you only look without buying, or when you enjoy a flashy sight. You say '눈요기하다' or '눈요기를 하다', and about a movie it can carry a slightly disappointed tone: nice to look at, not much else.

examples.en: The rice is scorching on the bottom of the pot.

examples.ko: 불이 세서 밥이 눋는 냄새가 나요.
examples.en: The heat is too high, and I smell rice scorching.
Oh, the rice is scorching. I'll turn the heat down.

examples.ko: 국이 눋지 않게 계속 저어 주세요.
examples.en: Please keep stirring so the soup doesn't scorch.

examples.ko: 전을 부치다가 바닥이 눋겠어요. 불 좀 줄여요.
examples.en: The pancake bottom is going to scorch. Please turn the heat down.
I turn off the heat before the rice scorches.

explain: 밥이나 국처럼 바닥에 붙어 거무스름하게 타는 것에 써요. 'ㄷ' 불규칙이라 '눋고, 눌어요, 눌은'으로 바뀌고, '눌어붙다'로도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when rice or soup sticks to the bottom and browns or burns. It is a ㄷ-irregular verb: 눋고, 눌어요, 눌은. People also say '눌어붙다'.

en: press something under; put a weight on

examples.ko: 바람에 날아가지 않게 책으로 종이를 눌러놓았어요.
examples.en: I weighed the paper down with a book so the wind wouldn't blow it away.

examples.ko: 김치 위에 돌을 눌러놓으면 국물에 잠겨요.
examples.en: If you put a stone on top of the kimchi, it stays under the brine.

examples.ko: 사진이 구겨지지 않게 두꺼운 책으로 눌러놔요.
examples.en: I press the photo under a thick book so it doesn't crease.

examples.ko: 접은 옷을 무거운 상자로 눌러놓고 잤어요.
examples.en: I put a heavy box on the folded clothes and went to sleep.

examples.ko: 꽃잎을 책 사이에 눌러놓았다가 책갈피로 썼어요.
examples.en: I pressed the petals between book pages and then used them as a bookmark.
I'll hold the moving boxes down from above so they don't shift.

explain: '누르다'는 잠깐 누르는 느낌이고, '눌러놓다'는 무거운 것으로 눌러서 그대로 두는 상태를 말해요. 말할 때는 '눌러놔요', '눌러놨어요'처럼 줄여요.
explain_en: '누르다' feels like pressing for a moment, while '눌러놓다' means pressing something with weight and leaving it that way. In speech it is shortened: 눌러놔요, 눌러놨어요.

en: pull low one's hat or cap

examples.en: I pulled my hat down low and went out.
I pulled my cap down deep to hide my face.

examples.ko: 야구 모자를 눌러쓴 남자가 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: A man with his baseball cap pulled low looked at me.
It's cold, so I pull my wool hat down over my ears.
If I pull my hat down in the morning, my hair gets flattened.
It was raining, so I pulled my raincoat hood down low.

explain: 모자 같은 것을 깊이 내려서 쓸 때 쓰고, 보통 '푹'과 잘 어울려요. 글씨를 힘주어 꾹꾹 쓸 때도 '눌러쓰다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when you pull a hat or similar item down low, often with '푹'. It is also used for writing with firm pressure, pressing hard on the paper.

examples.en: I meant to rest for a moment but just ended up staying put.

examples.ko: 친구 집에서 며칠 묵으려다 한 달이나 눌러앉았어요.
examples.en: I meant to stay at my friend's place a few days but ended up staying a whole month.
That player decided to stay with the team.
Is it okay if I just stay here?

examples.ko: 서울에 잠시 온 건데 십 년째 눌러앉아 살고 있어요.
examples.en: I only came to Seoul for a while, but I've ended up living here for ten years.
What do we do if the guest doesn't leave and just stays?

explain: 가려던 곳으로 안 가고 그 자리에 계속 머물게 될 때 써요. '머무르다'가 중립적인 말이라면, 이 말은 '어쩌다 오래 있게 됐다'는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when you don't go where you meant to and keep staying put. While '머무르다' is neutral, this word carries a feeling of ending up staying longer than planned.

examples.en: The sun is slowly sinking below the horizon.
I walked while watching the sunset slowly fade.

examples.ko: 산 너머로 해가 뉘엿뉘엿 저물어 가요.
examples.en: The sun is slowly setting behind the mountain.

examples.ko: 저녁이 되어 해가 뉘엿뉘엿 기울기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Evening came and the sun began to sink slowly.

examples.ko: 뉘엿뉘엿 해 지는 바다가 정말 예뻤어요.
examples.en: The sea with the sun slowly setting was really beautiful.

examples.ko: 퇴근길에 뉘엿뉘엿 지는 해를 한참 바라봤어요.
examples.en: On my way home from work, I watched the setting sun for a long time.

explain: 해가 지는 모습에만 쓰는 말이에요. '해가 뉘엿뉘엿 지다/넘어가다/기울다'처럼 말하고, 천천히 저무는 느낌이 있어서 달이나 사람의 움직임에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: This word is only for the sun setting. You say '해가 뉘엿뉘엿 지다/넘어가다/기울다', and it has a slow, gradual feel, so it is not used for the moon or for people's movements.

examples.en: I ate greasy food and now my stomach feels queasy.

examples.ko: 차를 오래 탔더니 속이 느글거리고 어지러워요.
examples.en: I rode in the car for a long time, and now I feel nauseous and dizzy.
I drank tea to settle my queasy stomach.

examples.ko: 아침부터 속이 느글거려서 밥을 못 먹었어요.
examples.en: My stomach has felt sick since morning, so I couldn't eat.

examples.ko: 튀김을 너무 많이 먹어서 느글거릴 것 같아요.
examples.en: I ate too much fried food, so I think I'm going to feel sick.

examples.ko: 속이 느글거릴 때는 매실차가 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Plum tea helps when your stomach feels queasy.

explain: '메스껍다'와 비슷하지만 느끼한 음식을 먹은 뒤의 속 불편함에 잘 어울려요. 보통 '속이 느글거리다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '메스껍다' (nauseous), but it fits the uneasy stomach after eating rich or greasy food. It is usually used as '속이 느글거리다'.

examples.en: The rain suddenly poured down and we all got soaked.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 느닷없는 고백에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by that person's out-of-the-blue confession.
My friend suddenly burst into tears and I was flustered.
While we were talking, I suddenly felt awkward.

examples.ko: 갑자기 전화해서 그런 말을 하다니 너무 느닷없어요.
examples.en: Calling out of nowhere and saying that is so abrupt.
I'm sorry for showing up without any notice.

explain: 대부분 '느닷없이'나 '느닷없는 + 명사'로 써요. '갑자기'는 단순히 때가 급할 때도 쓰지만, '느닷없다'는 앞뒤 흐름과 상관없이 불쑥 일어나서 당황스러운 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Most of the time it appears as '느닷없이' or '느닷없는 + noun'. '갑자기' can simply mean quickly, but '느닷없다' suggests something popping up with no connection to what came before, which feels startling.

examples.ko: 저는 걸음이 느려서 친구들이 느림뱅이라고 불러요.
examples.en: I walk slowly, so my friends call me a slowpoke.

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 밥 먹을 때 완전 느림뱅이예요.
examples.en: My son is a total slowpoke when he eats.
The slowpoke tortoise ended up beating the hare.

examples.ko: 일하는 게 느리다고 느림뱅이 취급하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't treat me like a dawdler just because I work slowly.
I'm always late because of that slowpoke.
I may be a slowpoke, but I'll see it through to the end.

explain: 행동이 느린 사람을 가볍게 놀릴 때 써요. '느림보'도 비슷하게 쓰고, 놀리는 느낌이 있어서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It is used to tease someone who is slow in their actions. '느림보' is used in a similar way. Since it has a teasing tone, avoid it with elders or people you've just met.

examples.en: I tied the string loosely, so it keeps coming undone.

examples.ko: 나사를 느슨히 조이면 흔들릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you tighten the screw only loosely, it may wobble.
I tied my hair loosely and sat down comfortably.
Nowadays the rules are being applied loosely.

examples.ko: 줄을 느슨히 잡으면 놓칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you hold the rope loosely, you might drop it.

examples.ko: 마음을 느슨히 먹으면 일이 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you let your guard down, things don't go well.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '느슨하게'라고도 말해요. 반대말은 '팽팽히'나 '단단히'이고, 끈·나사처럼 물건뿐 아니라 규칙이나 마음가짐이 풀린 것에도 써요.
explain_en: In everyday speech people also say '느슨하게'. Its opposites are '팽팽히' and '단단히', and it applies not only to things like strings and screws but also to relaxed rules or attitudes.

examples.en: On weekends I get up fairly late and have brunch.
I left home rather late and was late for the appointment.

examples.ko: 그는 느지막이 공부를 시작했지만 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: He started studying rather late in life, but he worked hard.
Today you can come to work a bit late.
I had a late lunch and then took a walk.
My mother got married rather late.

explain: '늦게'와 비슷하지만 서두르지 않는 여유로운 느낌이 있어요. 일어나다, 나가다, 먹다 같은 동작과 자주 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '늦게' (late), but it feels unhurried and relaxed. It is often paired with actions like waking up, going out and eating.

examples.en: I met a friend in the late afternoon.
It was getting late, so I hurried home.
I had a late breakfast and headed out slowly.

examples.ko: 약속 시간이 느지막하니 천천히 준비해도 돼요.
examples.en: The appointment is rather late, so you can get ready slowly.
I'm sorry for calling at such a late hour.
When I get off work late, I keep dinner simple.

explain: 시간이나 때가 꽤 늦은 것을 말하고, '느지막한 오후/아침'처럼 시간 이름 앞에 잘 붙어요. 일상에서는 부사 '느지막이'를 더 쉽게 만날 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a time that is fairly late and attaches easily before time words, as in '느지막한 오후/아침'. In daily life you will more easily meet the adverb '느지막이'.

examples.en: I fell and broke a rib.
The doctor took an X-ray of the rib area.
My ribs hurt, so it's hard to breathe.

examples.ko: 늑골 골절은 안정을 취하는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: For a rib fracture, resting is important.
I hurt my ribs while exercising and went to the hospital.
The area around my ribs keeps stabbing with pain.

explain: 일상에서는 '갈비뼈'라고 많이 말하고, '늑골'은 병원이나 뉴스, 의학 설명에서 자주 나와요. 고기를 말할 때의 '갈비'와는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: In daily life people often say '갈비뼈', while '늑골' appears often at hospitals, in the news and in medical explanations. It is different from '갈비', the meat dish.

examples.en: I dawdled and missed the bus.

examples.ko: 정부의 늑장 대응 때문에 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: The government was criticized for its slow response.
Don't dawdle first thing in the morning, hurry up.
My child dragged their feet and was late for school.

examples.ko: 늑장 출발 탓에 약속 시간에 늦었어요.
examples.en: Because of the late departure, I was late for the appointment.

examples.ko: 늑장 부릴 시간이 없어요, 빨리 와요.
examples.en: There's no time to dawdle, come quickly.

explain: '늑장을 부리다'라는 짝으로 가장 많이 쓰고, 뉴스에서는 '늑장 대응', '늑장 출동'처럼 나와요. '꾸물거리다'는 행동을 말하고, '늑장'은 해야 할 일을 일부러 늦추는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is most often paired as '늑장을 부리다', and in the news it appears as '늑장 대응' or '늑장 출동'. '꾸물거리다' describes the action of dawdling, while '늑장' suggests putting off what you should be doing.

en: one's old age; later years of one's life

examples.en: I want to go back to my hometown in my old age.
My grandfather learned to paint late in life.
Now that I'm in my later years, health matters most.

examples.ko: 그분은 늘그막에 자식 덕을 보셨다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that person was supported by their children in old age.
That person became a novelist late in life.

examples.ko: 늘그막의 외로움을 달래 줄 취미가 필요해요.
examples.en: You need a hobby that can ease the loneliness of old age.

explain: 대부분 '늘그막에'로 써서 나이가 들어 인생의 끝 무렵에 어떤 일을 한다는 뜻을 나타내요. '노년'은 중립적인 말이고, '늘그막'은 좀 더 말맛이 있는 우리말이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '늘그막에' to say someone does something late in life. '노년' is a neutral word, while '늘그막' is a more flavorful native Korean word.

examples.en: I was startled to see a red-banded snake on the mountain path.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 어릴 때 능구렁이를 잡아 본 적이 있대요.
examples.en: They say my grandfather caught a red-banded snake as a child.

examples.ko: 능구렁이는 산이나 밭 근처에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see red-banded snakes near mountains or fields.
The snake slowly disappeared into the grass.

examples.ko: 이 뱀은 몸에 붉은 무늬가 있는 능구렁이예요.
examples.en: This snake is a red-banded snake with red markings on its body.
My grandfather said he saw a red-banded snake in the yard.

explain: 뱀 이름이지만 사람에게 쓰면 속마음을 감추고 능청스럽게 행동하는 사람을 가리켜요. 칭찬이 아니라 조금 얄밉다는 느낌이라, 사람 앞에서 직접 말하는 건 조심해요.

phrases.example: 그 사장님은 능구렁이 같아서 속을 알 수 없어요.
phrases.en: That boss is sly, so you can't tell what he's thinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로는 순해 보여도 속이 깊고 음흉하다는 느낌으로, 사람을 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person who looks mild on the outside but is cunning and hard to read inside.

explain_en: It is a snake's name, but used about a person it refers to someone who hides their real thoughts and acts slyly. It is not praise but has a slightly annoyed tone, so be careful saying it to someone's face.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 능글거리며 농담을 해요.
examples.en: He always cracks jokes with a smug, sly manner.
Stop being so slick and tell me honestly.
It was annoying to see him grinning slyly after doing wrong.
My boss acts so slyly that it's uncomfortable to deal with him.
My younger sibling slyly asked me for pocket money.
That friend is annoying every time he acts all slick.

explain: 속은 따로 있으면서 겉으로 뻔뻔하게 웃거나 말하는 행동을 가리켜요. '능글맞다'가 그런 성질을 말한다면, '능글거리다'는 그렇게 행동하는 모습에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes grinning or talking shamelessly while hiding what you really think. While '능글맞다' describes that quality, '능글거리다' focuses on the act of behaving that way.

examples.en: He approached with a smug, sly smile.
My younger sibling lied with a sly grin.
He may look sly, but he's warm inside.

examples.ko: 말투가 너무 능글맞아서 정이 안 가요.
examples.en: His way of talking is so slick that I can't warm up to him.
Thanks to my cheeky friend, the mood loosened up.
Don't act so slick, answer seriously.

explain: 속마음을 숨기고 뻔뻔하고 능청스럽게 구는 사람이나 말투에 써요. 대체로 좀 얄밉다는 뜻이지만, 친한 사이에서는 장난스럽고 넉살 좋은 사람을 가볍게 말할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a person or tone that is shameless and slyly smooth while hiding true thoughts. It is mostly a bit annoying, but among close friends it can lightly describe a playful, brazen person.

examples.en: Try changing this sentence into the active voice.

examples.ko: 시험에 능동태와 피동태를 구별하는 문제가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The exam had a question about telling active and passive voice apart.
In an active-voice sentence, the subject performs the action.
The teacher wrote active-voice example sentences on the board.

examples.ko: 이 책은 능동태와 피동태를 쉽게 설명해 줘요.
examples.en: This book explains active and passive voice in an easy way.

examples.ko: 능동태로 쓰면 글이 더 힘 있게 읽혀요.
examples.en: Writing in the active voice makes the text read more forcefully.

explain: 문법 수업이나 시험에서 쓰는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 나오지 않아요. 짝이 되는 말은 '피동태'(피동문)이에요.
explain_en: This is a grammar-class and exam term that rarely comes up in everyday conversation. Its counterpart is '피동태' (passive voice).
